toml:
# Iridium STL (satellite time and location) bursts seen from an aircraft.
#
# An airliner at 10 km over the Atlantic, flying at 230 m/s heading west, sees a designed
# Iridium pass (781 km, 86.4 deg, peaking at 65 deg) on the STL band at 1621 MHz, and GPS L1
# C/A. Iridium's 66 satellites transmit PNT bursts inside one 90 ms frame at 1616-1626 MHz,
# with Doppler up to +/-36 kHz and a raw power 300 to 2400 times that of GPS (Resilient
# Navigation and Timing Foundation,
# https://rntfnd.org/wp-content/uploads/Recent-PNT-Improvements-and-Test-Results-Based-on-Low-Earth-Orbit-Satellites.pdf).
# The preset turns "300 times GPS" into an EIRP at 10 deg elevation with a flat pattern; the
# zenith then lands near the published "2400 times". The aircraft's own motion adds to the
# Doppler, and the report checks the closed-form Doppler and Doppler rate against a numerical
# derivative of the range.
#
# MODELLED. The spot beams, the burst schedule and the STL waveform are not modelled.
kind = "leo-pass"
name = "Iridium STL from an aircraft"
epoch = "2026-09-28T14:00:00"
duration_s = 900.0
step_s = 5.0

[user]
environment = "air"
lat_deg = 50.0
lon_deg = -30.0
height_m = 10000.0
speed_m_s = 230.0
heading_deg = 270.0

[[satellite]]
id = "Iridium-pass"
system = "iridium-stl"
max_elevation_deg = 65.0
tca_s = 450.0
direction = "descending"

[gnss]
constellation = "gps-baseline"
band = "L1"
summary:
LEO pass link budget, air user at 50.00, -30.00; 1 LEO satellite(s), 900 s window
  Iridium-pass [iridium-stl PUBLIC]: 781 km, max elevation 65.0 deg at 444 s, 750 s above the mask
         STL   1621.000 MHz: C/N0 peak 80.5 dB-Hz median 71.3 dB-Hz; |Doppler| max 35.4 kHz; iono 7.53 m
  GNSS gps-baseline L1: 8 in view, C/N0 38.2 dB-Hz to 51.1 dB-Hz (median 46.2 dB-Hz)
  LEO STL peak 80.5 dB-Hz is 34.3 dB above the GNSS median; above the strongest GNSS carrier for 750 s
